# The clean-room audit

<!-- Generated by `python -m larmorx_validation cleanroom-audit summary` from `docs/validation/clean-room-audit.json`; do not edit by hand. -->

The evidence, from records made at the time, that the clean-room originals in larmorx were written without their upstream's source. Dossier of 2026-11-13-freesurfer-batch-7; the records from 2026-10-09 11:38 UTC to 2026-11-13 09:55 UTC.

## What this page proves

Some of the tools larmorx re-implements are under licences that do not allow their code into an Apache-2.0 package (FSL's; AFNI's until its release 26.3.05; glibc's exact mathematics). For each, larmorx has two implementations ([licensing](../licensing.md)): a **replica**, a faithful port of the upstream source, kept in a separate package under the upstream's own licence; and a **clean-room original**, written only from a behaviour specification (`specs/`), the upstream's documentation, published papers and black-box runs of the upstream program, by agents that never saw the upstream source, the replica, or anything written from them. A specification is written by a different agent, which may read the source but describes only behaviour, mathematics and the command line, never code ([porting guide](../porting-guide.md) §1).

**The records.** Every agent that worked on larmorx was an AI agent (Claude Code), launched by one orchestrating session. Claude Code keeps a transcript of every session: each tool call (each file read, search, command and edit) with its result. The audit reads every transcript and lists, for each agent, what it read, searched, listed, ran and wrote. Each path is classified by a restriction table written from the project's rules, with the date each rule began to apply. Git's history says which agent made each commit of clean-room code: the commit hash the agent printed when it committed, or its commit command. For each clean-room original the question is: **did any agent that had seen restricted material of that tool's family edit its code afterwards?**

**The answer.** 281 commits changed clean-room code; 281 are attributed to the agent that made them (277 to clean-room implementers; the others are listed under [edits by other roles](#edits-of-clean-room-code-by-other-roles)). For every clean-room original below, no agent that had seen its upstream's source or its replica's code wrote its algorithms. The implementers' slips, lines of restricted material that a search printed, are each listed with their nature and judgement (35 calls, 10 of them not declared by their part): titles of defect entries, behaviour the specification already gave, another family's code, test-harness lines; none carries an upstream routine.

Code similarity is reported as extra evidence only ([below](#code-similarity-extra-evidence-no-threshold)): a figure, never a pass or a failure.

## What counts as restricted

The restriction table, from the project's rules (CLAUDE.md rule 1 and its agent rules, the [porting guide](../porting-guide.md) §1, [licensing](../licensing.md)). *Restricted since*: when its content became restricted by nature (the decision of 2026-10-09 for the upstream sources and the replicas; a file's first commit for a finding written from the source). *Named since*: when the rules first named it. An access between the two still counts: reading source-derived content is a contamination whatever the rules said that day.

| rule | what | family | restricted since | named since | basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R01 | FSL's source (crates-nc/fsl-source, the installation's src, include, pkgs, its scripts and Python modules read as text) | FSL | 2026-10-09 | 2026-10-09 | CLAUDE.md rule 1 (8d332534); decision log 2026-10-09 |
| R02 | AFNI's source (MCW and NIH files alike; the clean-room originals stay clean after the CC BY 4.0 move of 2026-10-29) | AFNI | 2026-10-09 | 2026-10-09 | decision log 2026-10-09; CLAUDE.md rule 1 (8d332534) |

**Allowed, and logged by kind:** black-box runs of the original programs (FSL's, AFNI's, ANTs', FreeSurfer's, fMRIPrep's), their `-help` and documentation, permissive upstream source (ANTs, ITK, nibabel, SciPy, numpy, OpenBLAS, CORE-MATH, Arm's routines, nitransforms, fMRIPrep and its libraries), `specs/`, the clean-room code, oracle outputs and data.

**How each restricted access weighs** (the verdicts' levels):

| level | meaning |
|---|---|
| content | content of restricted material shown or copied |
| possible | a path of restricted material in a script the agent ran (the file may have been opened) |
| scope | restricted material inside a search's scope, no line of it printed |
| names | names of restricted files only |
| build | the replica compiled or its tests run (no file shown) |
| mention | a restricted path named in a command's arguments (nothing shown) |
| replica-run | the replica program run as a black box (its compiled output) |
| build-cache | the replica's build outputs copied, listed or removed (a build cache) |
| metadata | a replica crate's licence, notice or package metadata |
| clean-writer | notes or reports written only by clean-room implementers (and the briefs) |
| register headings | titles of restricted defect entries only (the register's open table describes every entry) |
| register body lines | lines of a restricted section's text |

*Whose material:* **this family** (the tool's own upstream, its replica or findings about it, while the rule applied); **another family** (for example AFNI's replica seen by an agent that wrote FSL code); **before the rule applied**; **written by clean-room implementers only** (other parts' notes whose every writer was a clean-room implementer of the same kind, or the orchestrator's brief).

## Per clean-room original

### 3dTshift

- **Family:** AFNI. **Edited** from 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-11; **commits:** 13 (by role: clean-room implementer 11, integration 1, orchestrator 1).

## What the evidence cannot see

- **Programs' own reads.** A command's reads are seen through the paths it names and the output it printed: cargo, pytest and scripts read files the transcript does not list. A compile error in a replica crate or a failing replica test would print source lines: none was found in the implementers' outputs (the compiler's diagnostics are parsed), but outputs written to log files and never shown are not in the transcripts (some relays ran their gates that way).
- **Listings.** The names printed by `find` and `ls` are not parsed (the search tools' are): names-level slips of that kind are seen only through the command's arguments, and they are names only, by definition.
- **Replica suites the briefs allowed.** The FLIRT, FAST, topup and fslmaths clean-room briefs named the replica's parity suite for its cases and mechanics. Their implementers' reads of it are allowed by their briefs; the suites were written by replica authors and are not judged line by line.
- **Roles.** Roles are read from the launch descriptions and the briefs; four were settled by hand. Every agent that touched clean-room code was checked by reading its brief's role sentence.
- **Searches of one file.** A search of a single file prints no file name: the register's are checked by content against every version of its restricted lines, every other restricted file's against that file's lines today (a line that changed since would not be recognised).
- **Before the first record.** The repository's first 15 minutes (its root commit, 2026-10-09) precede the first transcript record; no clean-room code existed then. Agents without a harness worktree in their metadata (early agents and relays) are attributed by the commit hashes they printed or by their commit commands.
- **The briefs.** The briefs were written by the orchestrator, who reads source to merge: the clean-room parts' briefs hold no line of a restricted register section and no line of a source-derived finding (checked against every version), and name upstream source files only in their forbidden lists.
- **Live transcripts.** Transcripts newer than the archive of 2026-11-05 were read where Claude Code keeps them; they still grow and are deleted after 30 days. From this audit on, every merge copies its part's transcripts into the archive with their SHA-256 before it runs the audit.

## Recommendations

1. Name the replica program as an allowed black box in the porting guide (every FSL clean-room part runs it), and say which replica suite modules a clean-room brief may name.
2. Since the AFNI replicas moved into crates/ (2026-10-29), a search over crates/ prints their lines: briefs should ask for `grep ... crates/ --exclude-dir=larmorx-afni-replica` (two undeclared slips of this kind).
3. Exclude folders with `--exclude-dir` rather than by filtering a search's output: a filter on `^./` fails when grep prints names without `./` (the AFNI-26 slip).
4. Run the audit at every merge (scripts/orchestration/cleanroom-audit-merge.sh): it archives the part's transcripts and stops the merge on any unjudged edit of clean-room code after restricted material of the tool's family.

## How to re-run

On the machine that holds the transcripts (the outputs are private: they hold absolute paths and the account name; they stay in `<workspace>/archive/clean-room-audit/<date>/`), each step inside a memory box:

```bash
D=<workspace>/archive/clean-room-audit/<date>
scripts/orchestration/boxed.sh 24 scripts/orchestration/lxv.sh . cleanroom-audit scan --out $D/scan --jobs 12
scripts/orchestration/lxv.sh . cleanroom-audit verdicts --scan $D/scan --out $D/verdicts
scripts/orchestration/boxed.sh 24 scripts/orchestration/lxv.sh . cleanroom-audit similarity --out $D/similarity --wide --jobs 12
scripts/orchestration/lxv.sh . cleanroom-audit summary --dossier $D --verbatim $D/verbatim.md
scripts/orchestration/lxv.sh . cleanroom-audit gate --verdicts $D/verdicts
```

The scan reads every transcript (the archives `<workspace>/archive/*session-transcripts*/` and Claude Code's own folder) in about 15 seconds; the verdicts take seconds; the similarity about 15 minutes with `--wide` (every C and C++ file of AFNI's and FSL's trees). The summary writes `docs/validation/clean-room-audit.json` (the public facts) and this page; `cleanroom-audit summary --check` renders the committed facts and compares them with this page. At every merge, `scripts/orchestration/cleanroom-audit-merge.sh` archives the part's transcripts with their SHA-256 and runs the scan, the verdicts and the gate, which stops the merge when a clean-room original was edited after restricted material of its family was seen, unless the item is judged in `validation/cleanroom-audit/judgements.toml`.

Made from the scan `scan` and the verdicts of the repository at `5b4c1f09`.
